description: Add an optional motor variant to the gripper: the gripper base can alternatively be driven by the SO-101 arm's motor, the Feetech STS3215 servo, instead of the RobStride RS00. Make the motor a selectable parameter (motor = RS00 | STS3215) with the right mount, gear or horn interface and cable routing for each, built on the latest Base (see AGENTS.md hardware notes and the Gripper/Handle/Base scheme). Also record joint positions from the STS3215 servo while the gripper is used by hand, for data collection.

results.identified_issue: motor_sts is numeric (params.py only takes numbers). The STS geometry lives in gripper.scad's 'Base 11' block: sts_frame2d (u along the body, w across), sts_seat (cut from base), sts3215 (reference model), sts_cable (keep-out). m_out_pcd/holes/screws pick which output the pinion bolts to. The hub still uses motor_out_pcd because J6 is always an RS00. Base underside = rail plane. The hump uses a through-window, not a pocket, because an underside pocket would be a bridge and fail the overhang check. The spigot assert now checks only the part of the screw that actually reaches the spigot. Dimensions come from STS3215_03a.step (horn holes 2.5 mm on 14 PCD = M3, case holes 1.5 mm = M2 per the SO-101 guide's M2x6). The servo-model rails are inset 0.01 mm because Clipper-quantised 2D left non-manifold slivers against the body box. export_models/check_geometry/genus/live_render drop the reBot mount parts when motor_sts=1. Verified: RS00 mode prints match v310 triangle sets; RS00 71/71 and STS 59/59 checks; genus OK. Not verified: real servo fit, M2 depth, back-drive force, record_grip on hardware. Pre-existing unrelated failure: test_gripper_poses has no poses.js entry for v306.
results.summary: Base 11: the motor is now a switch, motor_sts (0 = RS00, 1 = STS3215). The STS3215 drives the pinion through its horn and screws to the base by its case. record_grip.py records finger angle from the back-driven servo.
results.detailed_description:
Base 11 (v311_generalist_motor_choice) is Base 10 with one new parameter, motor_sts. It's a 0/1 slider on the Tune panel, because params.json only holds numbers.

motor_sts 0 is the RobStride RS00: Base 10 exactly, wrist mount and arm included. Every printed part comes out with the same triangles as Base 10, and Base 10's 71 checks pass.

motor_sts 1 is the Feetech STS3215, the SO-101 servo, and it's what Base 11 shows by default. I measured it from The Robot Studio's own STEP (SO-ARM100, Apache-2.0) and used the SO-101 assembly guide's screws:
- Horn: the same 34-tooth pinion sits on the servo's 20 mm round horn, with 4 countersunk M3 into the horn's 4 holes. A recess clears the horn's centre screw. The ratio is 1:1.
- Mount: the base sits on the servo's two front rails, with 4 M2x8 into the case. The heads sit in recesses below the handle-gears. The label hump on the servo's face stands up into a window cut straight through the base, so the base still prints flat with no bridge. The servo body runs straight down under the pinion, so the gripper gets no wider.
- Cable: the bus cable plugs into the servo's back face and leaves straight back. There's a 14 mm keep-out for the plug and its bend, and it is clear of every part at every swing.
- No reBot wrist mount with this motor: the bracket bolts to the RS00's back face, so the STS3215 gripper is hand-held.
- 59/59 geometry checks pass, including 9 new servo checks.

Data collection: record_grip.py switches the servo's torque off so your hand back-drives it. It reads the servo's raw position through LeRobot's Feetech bus at 100 Hz and writes a CSV of t_s, raw, servo_deg, finger_deg (0 closed to 30 open, about 11.4 counts per degree). You close the fingers and press Enter to zero it. Run it with: conda activate lerobot, then python3 record_grip.py --port <port> --id 1. A new servo is ID 1; the SO-101 gripper is ID 6.

What to check:
- I had no servo here. record_grip.py only ran with --fake, and I built LeRobot's bus without connecting to a port.
- Buy the leader-arm gearing for hand use: C046 (1/147) or C044 (1/191). The follower's C001 (1/345) is stiff to back-drive.
- Two things in the model are cheats. Their STEP has the label hump 1.1 mm under the horn's rim, so I cut the hump round the horn. The far M2 holes are only 2 mm from the base's edge.
- In the preview, tuning motor_sts to 0 shows the RS00 drive but not the wrist mount, because the exported part list is the STS3215's.
- I also added the STS3215 option to AGENTS.md's hardware notes.

summary: The gripper base design only supports the RobStride RS00 motor, and there is no option to use the SO-101 arm's Feetech STS3215 servo. Add a selectable motor parameter (RS00 or STS3215) with the correct mount, horn interface and cable routing, built on the latest Base, and record STS3215 joint positions during hand use for data collection.
